entities.summary:
Hartwig I. von Stade was a German count and archbishop who played a significant role in the medieval Holy Roman Empire.

He was born around 1120 and succeeded his father Rudolf I, Margrave of the Nordmark, as Count of Stade.

In 1147, Hartwig I. von Stade was elected Archbishop of Bremen, a position he held until his death in 1168.

During his tenure, he oversaw several significant events, including the Stade Peace of 1147, which settled a long-standing conflict between the County of Stade and the Bishopric of Bremen.

Hartwig I. von Stade also played a key role in the development of the Bremen Cathedral, which became one of the most important architectural landmarks of the Middle Ages.

His legacy as a mediator and administrator has endured, with the Stade Peace of 1147 remaining a significant example of medieval diplomacy.

"The Stade Peace is a testament to Hartwig I. von Stade's skill as a mediator, one that has stood the test of time." - Medieval historian, Richard Barber.
